edits.content:
## MANDATORY ANSWER LINE (do this before every answer)
Before the `<answer>` tags write exactly one line, and no more than one:
`Type: <the noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, matches the clue's singular/plural, and is not a word from the clue>`
If Check fails, change the candidate and rewrite the line. This line covers the Type/Constraints/Form check below. A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) still beats your own knowledge.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content: - SOURCE PRIORITY: archive/flashcard/dump line that reproduces the clue and gives an answer > reference passage > forum, quiz-user or contestant reply > your own guess. A lower tier never beats a higher one. Copy the archived answer exactly as shown, including a leading 'a/an/the' and any trailing generic noun. Quote the matched line before the answer tags.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Archive and forum dumps are often run-on with no separator ('...<clue text> ANSWER This "next clue"...'). When a passage repeats the clue's exact wording, the word(s) right after the clue's last word, up to where the next clue begins, are the archived answer. If it is shorter than the longer name in other passages, copy the SHORT archived form.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - EXEMPTION: the shortening, article-dropping and delete-clue-words rules below apply ONLY when no verbatim archive answer exists (Rule 3). If an archive line gives the answer, copy it as shown.

edits.target: If the clue says 'this vitamin', answer with just the letter. If the clue names a group or band, give the group's name only.
For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
edits.content: For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form the passages repeat, preferring a formal given name over a diminutive ('Patricia', not 'Patty') when a passage gives it.

edits.target: - When the clue says 'this country / this vitamin / this man / one of these ...', the answer is the thing that phrase stands for. Do not copy a proper noun or phrase already in the clue.
edits.content: - When the clue says 'this country / this vitamin / this man / one of these ...', the answer is the thing that phrase stands for. ANCHOR GATE: any region, town, river, product or person named in the clue is an anchor, never the answer. Reject a candidate that is a word from the clue or merely restates one. A place named next to 'this country/state/city' means the larger country/state/city that contains it. SUBSTITUTION TEST: put the candidate into the clue's blank; if the result is the wrong kind of thing for the clue's 'this <noun>' or repeats a clue noun, reject it. The Rule 4 keep-head-noun exception applies only when the clue's 'this <type>' is itself the head of the named entity ('this purchase' -> Gadsden Purchase), not when the clue's noun is a different category (city, acid, person).

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a quoted catchphrase or exclamation asks for the show, film or character that owns it, not a passage title (episode, song, video) that merely contains the quote.
- A clue about what 'he/she' did or wrote ('he wrote an explanation of why he would...') asks for the PERSON; the work (poem, letter, painting) is an anchor, never the answer.
- A clue saying a title or phrase was 'changed', 'altered' or 'parodied' asks for the ORIGINAL, unaltered title or phrase, not the altered version shown in the passages.
- 'The alliance / league / union / guild / chain of these <adjective> <businesses/people>' asks for the generic PLURAL member noun, not the organisation's proper name from the passages ('the guild of these Swiss watchmakers' -> 'watchmakers').

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - Nickname or definition clues: weight passages by kind, not by count. A passage that lists the term under its owner (a nickname list 'Kansas: Cyclone State', a glossary entry) beats many passages that use the same word in another sense (teams, schools, products, fan pages). For a bare definition, answer the term the glossaries tie to that exact role, not a related subordinate or different role (an assistant, a deputy).

edits.target: When passages are noisy, use your own knowledge of sports terms and idioms.
edits.content: - Variant: when one half is a title or phrase with a quoted word ('a Helen Reddy "Dawn"'), treat the quoted word as the neighbor of a blank ('___ Dawn') and test the same blank word against the other half. Answer with that single shared word, with no quotes and none of the title text the clue already states.

edits.target: look for the passage that glosses it ('locally referred to as lambi') and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
look for the passage that glosses it ('locally referred to as lambi') and answer with the common English name (Conch). The reverse also holds: when the clue gives a translation or etymology ('whose name is Greek for "leaf"') and asks for the term, find the passages that pair that quoted gloss with a term and answer with that term.
- Opening interjections ('Hallelujah!') and 'Whether it's A or B' asides are decoration. They do not ask you to choose A or B. Answer with the single underlying thing the factual core describes.

edits.target: ## Rule 1: Questions are Jeopardy-style clues; always answer with the missing entity
edits.content: - A bare 'YEAR: descriptor' fragment ('1968: Starring <star>') or a clue naming a star, network and year asks for the WORK (film, series, song) that the passages repeatedly tie to all those anchors. Give the bare title, not the star, the year or a label like 'film'.

edits.target: - For titles, give the standard title without quotation marks and keep internal punctuation as written in the context ('M*A*S*H', not 'MASH film').
edits.content:
- QUOTED TITLE FRAGMENT: when the clue puts one word of a work's title in quotes and asks for the work ('about this "Express"', 'this "...Road"'), the quoted word is PART of the answer. Give the full standard title as the passages repeat it, including a leading 'The' if they show it. The delete-clue-words test applies to separate modifiers, not to a quoted word that is the tail of a title.
- PART-OF-NAME REQUESTS: when the clue asks only for a part ('Last name of the brothers who...', 'surname'), answer with exactly that part. The full-name rule applies only when the clue asks for the person.
- SPELLING VARIANTS: when the passages spell the answer several ways ('phyllo' / 'filo'), use the variant in the passage sentence that matches the clue's wording and is most frequent across passages. Give it as a bare word.

edits.target: the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - 'Known by this trade / brand name' (a generic drug or product already named in the clue): answer with ONE brand name, the one most repeated and listed first across the passages, in the passages' spelling. Do not answer with the generic name from the clue or a list of brands.
